biography.plain_text: William Randall 'Randy' Holloway was an American manufacturing executive and longtime head of Holloway Sportswear. After gaining control of the family enterprise in the late 1970s, he directed its Ohio-based athletic-apparel operations until a private-equity sale in 2006. He later retired in Florida following the transaction and died there at 74.

long_biography.plain_text:
J.H. 'Bus' Holloway created an Ohio sportswear concern and gave each of his children a minority interest. His son William Randall, known as Randy, became its successor. In 1978, Randy financed a $1,015,443 purchase of his father's majority block, then assumed control of a closely held enterprise producing uniforms, letterman jackets, fleece and outerwear.

Nearly three decades of stewardship ended when Linsalata Capital Partners acquired Holloway Group and Holloway Sportswear in 2006. The business was combined with Augusta Sportswear, while Holloway left corporate life for Fort Lauderdale. He died at 74. Family, friends and former employees described an energetic traveller and keen pilot whose direct manner was matched by generosity, humour and a willingness to mentor colleagues.
long_biography.html:
J.H. 'Bus' Holloway created an Ohio sportswear concern and gave each of his children a minority interest. His son William Randall, known as Randy, became its successor. In 1978, Randy financed a $1,015,443 purchase of his father's majority block, then assumed control of a closely held enterprise producing uniforms, letterman jackets, fleece and outerwear.

Nearly three decades of stewardship ended when Linsalata Capital Partners acquired Holloway Group and Holloway Sportswear in 2006. The business was combined with Augusta Sportswear, while Holloway left corporate life for Fort Lauderdale. He died at 74. Family, friends and former employees described an energetic traveller and keen pilot whose direct manner was matched by generosity, humour and a willingness to mentor colleagues.
